concepts.name: SQLite WAL journal mode

concepts.name: SQLite busy timeout
concepts.description: A per-connection setting that makes SQLite wait up to a set number of milliseconds for a lock before failing with SQLITE_BUSY.

concepts.name: SQLite foreign keys pragma
concepts.description: SQLite leaves foreign key enforcement off by default. PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON must be set on each new connection for constraints to be enforced.

concepts.name: Retry on SQLITE_BUSY
concepts.description: Application-level retry loop that re-runs an operation when SQLite still reports busy after busy_timeout expires, and rethrows any other error immediately.

concepts.name: Safe retry of rolled-back transactions
concepts.description: A transaction that fails with a busy error has rolled back, so re-running it is safe only if the retried function wraps the whole transaction and has no side effects outside the database.

concepts.name: Backoff between retries
concepts.description: Waiting between retry attempts, with the delay growing or varying by attempt, so competing clients do not retry in lockstep and collide again.

concepts.name: Multi-process SQLite concurrency
concepts.description: Several processes (server, hooks, CLI, dashboard) share one SQLite file. Safety comes from WAL, lock waiting and retries together, because SQLite allows only one writer at a time.
